concepts.name: Himalayan System: Origin, Structure, and Parallel Ranges
key_dimensions: Tectonic origin via Indo-Eurasian plate collision and age comparison with other fold mountains
Three parallel ranges: Greater Himalayas, Lesser Himalayas (Himachal), and Outer Himalayas (Shivaliks) — distinguishing characteristics
Asymmetry of slopes (gentle northern vs steep southern) and its climatic/drainage implications
UPSC trap: Distinguishing Trans-Himalayan ranges (Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar) from the main Himalayan system

concepts.name: Andes Mountains: Longest Continental Mountain Range
key_dimensions: Tectonic setting: Subduction of Nazca Plate under South American Plate — comparison with Himalayan collision tectonics
Countries traversed (7 countries) and highest peaks (Aconcagua as highest outside Asia)
Altiplano plateau formation, role in Amazon and Atacama climate systems
UPSC trap: Andes as fold mountains vs block mountains; volcanic activity along the range (part of Pacific Ring of Fire)

concepts.name: Alps: Formation, Passes, and Geopolitical Significance
key_dimensions: Formation through collision of African and Eurasian plates; comparisons with Himalayas in age and height
Major passes: St. Bernard, Brenner, Simplon — their historical and trade route significance
River systems originating from Alps: Rhine, Rhone, Po, Danube
UPSC trap: Distinguishing Alpine folding from Hercynian folding; which European ranges are older remnants

concepts.name: Rockies vs Appalachians: New vs Old Mountain Comparison
key_dimensions: Rockies as young fold mountains (Laramide orogeny) vs Appalachians as ancient eroded mountains
Role in North American continental divide and watershed separation (Pacific vs Atlantic drainage)
Appalachians' role in early American settlement patterns and coal deposits
UPSC trap: Appalachians are among the world's oldest mountain ranges — examinees often confuse 'old' with 'low'; height vs age relationship

concepts.name: Karakoram Range: Strategic and Geographic Significance
key_dimensions: Location relative to Himalayas, Hindukush, and Pamir — the 'Pamir Knot' as a convergence point
Highest concentration of high peaks (K2, Gasherbrum, Broad Peak) and largest non-polar glaciers (Siachen, Baltoro)
Geopolitical significance: India-Pakistan-China tripoint, Siachen conflict zone
UPSC trap: K2 is NOT in the Himalayas — it is in Karakoram; confusion between Karakoram Pass and Khyber Pass

concepts.name: Hindukush and Pamir: The 'Roof of the World' Convergence
key_dimensions: Pamir Knot as the meeting point of Himalayas, Karakoram, Hindukush, Tian Shan, and Kunlun
Hindukush's role as a historical invasion corridor into the Indian subcontinent (Khyber Pass)
Wakhan Corridor geopolitics (Afghanistan, China border strip)
UPSC trap: Pamir is a plateau (not a range per se) — the 'knot' concept and which ranges radiate from it

concepts.name: Tian Shan and Altai: Central Asian Mountain Systems
key_dimensions: Tian Shan ('Heavenly Mountains') location across China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan — role in Silk Route geography
Altai as the source of major rivers: Ob, Irtysh — significance for Siberian drainage
Distinction between Tian Shan (fold mountain) and Altai (complex orogenic system)
UPSC trap: Altai mountains as the boundary concept between Central Asia and Siberia; often confused with Ural Mountains in terms of continental divide role

concepts.name: Ural Mountains: Europe-Asia Continental Divide
key_dimensions: Role as the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia — why this boundary is geographical, not tectonic
Ancient (Caledonian/Hercynian) eroded mountains — mineral wealth (iron ore, copper, platinum)
Ural River (not Ural Mountains) as the southern extension of this boundary
UPSC trap: Urals are low-elevation ancient mountains — examinees confuse them with being a significant topographic barrier; they are NOT a climate divide

concepts.name: Atlas Mountains: Africa's Northern Fold Mountains
key_dimensions: Location across Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia — part of Alpine-Himalayan fold mountain belt
Sub-ranges: High Atlas, Middle Atlas, Anti-Atlas, Tell Atlas, Saharan Atlas
Role as a barrier between Mediterranean climate and Sahara Desert
UPSC trap: Atlas Mountains are fold mountains (not the African Rift system); often confused with being part of the Great Rift Valley geology

concepts.name: Ethiopian Highlands and East African Rift System
key_dimensions: Formation through rifting and volcanic activity — NOT fold mountains (contrast with Atlas)
Role as the 'water tower of Africa' — source of Blue Nile, Awash River
Relationship between rift valleys and block mountains (horst and graben structure)
UPSC trap: Distinguishing between fold mountains and block mountains in Africa; Kilimanjaro and Kenya as volcanic peaks, not part of a range

concepts.name: Caucasus Mountains: Europe's Highest Range and Geopolitical Divide
key_dimensions: Greater Caucasus vs Lesser Caucasus — Mount Elbrus (highest peak in Europe by one convention)
Europe-Asia boundary debate: Ural vs Caucasus convention and its implications
Geopolitical significance: Russia, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan conflicts (Nagorno-Karabakh, South Ossetia)
UPSC trap: Whether Mont Blanc (Alps) or Elbrus (Caucasus) is the highest in Europe — depends on which Europe-Asia boundary is used

concepts.name: Zagros and Elburz Mountains: Iran's Tectonic Framework
key_dimensions: Zagros formed by Arabian-Eurasian plate collision — fold-and-thrust belt with major oil deposits
Elburz (Alborz) separating the Caspian Sea lowlands from the Iranian Plateau
Mount Damavand (Elburz) as the highest volcano in Asia and highest peak in Middle East
UPSC trap: Zagros fold mountains and their relationship to Persian Gulf oil formation; confusion between Zagros and Taurus (Turkey)

concepts.name: Scandinavian Mountains (Scandes): Caledonian Relicts
key_dimensions: Part of the ancient Caledonian orogeny — same fold system as Scottish Highlands and Appalachians (pre-continental drift connection)
Role in creating fjords through glacial erosion on the western Norwegian coast
Continental divide for Scandinavian rivers flowing to North Sea vs Baltic Sea
UPSC trap: Caledonian mountains on both sides of the Atlantic as evidence of Pangaea — the connection between Appalachians, Caledonians, and Scandes

concepts.name: Mountain Types: Fold, Block, Volcanic, and Residual — Classification and Examples
key_dimensions: Fold mountains (compressional): Himalayas, Andes, Alps, Rockies — tectonic settings (collision vs subduction)
Block mountains (horst): Vosges, Black Forest, Sierra Nevada (USA) — formed by tensional forces
Volcanic mountains: Kilimanjaro, Fuji, Mauna Kea — distinction between shield and composite volcanoes
UPSC trap: Sierra Nevada (USA) is a block mountain (tilted fault block), NOT a fold mountain — commonly confused; Residual mountains like Aravallis as worn-down ancient folds

concepts.name: Pacific Ring of Fire Mountain Systems: Volcanic Arcs and Cordilleras
key_dimensions: Western cordilleras of the Americas (Rockies-Andes system) as continental margin mountains from subduction
Island arc mountain systems: Japanese Alps, Philippine highlands formed by oceanic subduction
Distinction between continental volcanic arcs and island arcs in terms of geology and hazard profiles
UPSC trap: Not all Ring of Fire mountains are island arcs — the Andes are continental but still part of the Ring; Mount St. Helens vs Fuji as different volcanic types

concepts.name: Orographic Effect and Mountain Ranges as Climatic Barriers
key_dimensions: Rain shadow effect: Western Ghats/Deccan, Andes/Atacama, Himalayas/Tibetan Plateau
Himalayas as a climatic barrier: blocking Central Asian cold winds and confining monsoon — comparison with Alps which do NOT create similar monsoon-blocking effect
Foehn winds (Alps), Chinook winds (Rockies), Zonda winds (Andes) — warm, dry winds on leeward sides
UPSC trap: The Tibetan Plateau's role in intensifying the South Asian Monsoon — often attributed only to Himalayas; the plateau heating mechanism

concepts.name: Mountain Passes: Strategic, Trade, and Military Significance
key_dimensions: Himalayan passes: Nathu La, Shipki La, Zoji La, Bara Lacha La — country connections and strategic importance
Karakoram Pass vs Khyber Pass: location, country, strategic use — a classic UPSC confusion pair
Global passes: Khyber (Afghanistan-Pakistan), Bolan (Pakistan), St. Bernard (Alps), Brenner (Alps)
UPSC trap: Zoji La connects Kashmir to Ladakh (NOT India to China); Nathu La connects Sikkim to Tibet (China) — precise geographic accuracy tested

concepts.name: Highest Peaks by Continent and Mountain Range Superlatives
key_dimensions: Seven Summits: Everest (Asia), Aconcagua (South America), Denali (North America), Kilimanjaro (Africa), Elbrus or Mont Blanc (Europe — disputed), Vinson (Antarctica), Puncak Jaya (Australia/Oceania)
Distinction: Highest peak vs highest base-to-summit (Mauna Kea) vs furthest from Earth's center (Chimborazo)
Top 10 highest peaks: All in Himalayan-Karakoram system — knowing which are in Himalayas vs Karakoram
UPSC trap: K2 is in Karakoram, NOT Himalayas; Kangchenjunga is the highest peak in India; Godwin-Austen is another name for K2

concepts.name: Tibetan Plateau: The 'Third Pole' and Its Global Significance
key_dimensions: Formation as an uplifted block between the converging plates — highest and largest plateau in the world
Role as the origin of major Asian rivers: Indus, Ganga (Gangotri glacier), Brahmaputra, Mekong, Yangtze, Yellow River
'Third Pole' concept: largest freshwater reservoir outside polar ice caps — climate change vulnerability
UPSC trap: Brahmaputra originates in Tibet (as Tsangpo) and flows EAST before bending — not a common knowledge point; Tibetan Plateau is NOT a mountain range but is bounded by them

concepts.name: Mountain Glaciers: Distribution, Significance, and Climate Change Linkage
key_dimensions: Major glaciated mountain regions: Himalayas-Karakoram, Andes (Patagonia), Alps, Rockies, Alaska Range
Karakoram anomaly: Some glaciers advancing while Himalayan glaciers retreat — a current affairs-geography overlap
Glacier lake outburst floods (GLOFs) in Himalayan region — Uttarakhand, Nepal, Bhutan vulnerability
UPSC trap: Siachen Glacier (Karakoram, NOT Himalayas) is the world's highest battlefield; Gangotri glacier recession rate as an example of climate indicator
